editor_note: This issue looks at how shocks travel through global markets. Three papers examine the United States as a source: Treasury bond supply, monetary policy and the global financial cycle, and the safe-haven status of government bonds. Two papers turn to geopolitics, separating feared from realised energy disruptions and tracing how euro area sovereign bond holders react to geopolitical risk. A further group covers market structure and policy design, with evidence on offshore forwards in emerging-market currencies, Bank of Japan equity purchases and stablecoin flows. Taken together, the papers show that the dollar, investor composition and expectations often matter as much as the initial shock.
selection_rationale: I prioritised the 10/10 papers on US rates and dollar spillovers, EM FX plumbing, safe-haven behaviour and central-bank balance sheets, then added energy-shock and geopolitical-risk papers because they are the month's dominant macro theme. The pick has three Transversal, three DM and two EM papers, and mixes IMF, NBER, BIS, Fed and ECB sources. I left out the IMF paper on US long rates and EM local-currency bonds because it overlaps with the bond supply spillovers paper, and I took the BIS NDF paper instead for EM. I also left out strong 9/10 DM pieces, such as the AER inflation papers, the sovereign-bank nexus note, the Treasury dealer balance sheet note and the tariff pass-through post, because their topics were more specialised or more US-centric, or the issue was already weighted toward IMF and NBER output. The thin-abstract BIS 'Inflation after the Iran war' was also left out in favour of the more fully documented IMF energy-shock paper.

papers.headline: U.S. Treasury supply shocks lift foreign yields and depress global output
papers.selection_reason: Scores 10/10 and quantifies how US Treasury supply shocks pass through to foreign long yields (about 7bp per 10bp), FX and growth, which bears directly on rates and FX positioning.

papers.headline: Offshore NDF order flow moves onshore spot rates in emerging markets
papers.selection_reason: Scores 10/10 and uses transaction-level cleared NDF data for ten EM currencies to show how offshore flow drives onshore spot and the forward spread, making it the issue's core EM FX paper.

papers.headline: A model linking U.S. monetary policy to global risk premia through dollar funding
papers.selection_reason: Scores 10/10 and gives a general equilibrium account of how US tightening raises the global price of risk through dollar-short arbitrageurs, a framework for FX and risk-premium spillovers.

papers.headline: Did government bonds lose their safe-haven role during the Middle East escalation?
papers.selection_reason: Scores 10/10 and asks whether DM government bonds still act as safe havens when an energy shock raises inflation, a live question for rates and cross-asset desks.

papers.headline: Bank of Japan stock purchases: effects depend on yield curve control
papers.selection_reason: Scores 10/10 and offers clean causal evidence on how BoJ equity purchases interact with yield curve control, adding an advanced-economy central-bank-balance-sheet angle.

papers.headline: Fear of energy shortages moves prices before supply disruptions arrive
papers.selection_reason: Scores 9/10 and separates realised oil and gas supply disruptions from geopolitical-risk shocks, with implications for inflation and central banks in the 2026 Middle East energy episode.

papers.headline: How euro area sovereign bond holders respond to geopolitical risk
papers.selection_reason: Scores 9/10 and uses granular ECB holdings data to show how investor types react to geopolitical risk in high-debt euro area sovereigns, adding an ECB source and a euro-area credit and spreads view.

papers.headline: Stablecoin holdings rise after capital controls and currency crises
papers.selection_reason: Scores 9/10 and covers 188 countries to show how capital controls and currency crises drive stablecoin flows and dollarisation, a second EM paper on a topic that is new for EM FX and flows.
